The executable is still `cholesky`, no files were added, and it builds with no warnings under nvcc 12.0 and MPI. It uses CUDA, MPI and OpenMP unconditionally, and adds no libraries beyond those.\n\n**One behaviour change to know about:** `-r` prints a hash of the result. The new code does not reproduce the original's bits, so that hash will differ for most sizes. Validation metrics match the original's printed absolute errors exactly at every size I tested (n = 37 to 1000). The relative errors differ at roundoff level (around 1e-14 for tiny elements), and all cases pass the 1e-6 tolerance. The original's own result is not reproducible at the bit level: GCC fuses some multiply-adds and not others, and `-ffp-contract=off` gives yet another hash. I therefore treat `-r` hashes as tolerance-level, not exact. If external validation needs exact hashes, tell me and I'll change the generation path.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** rows are dealt in 128-row blocks, block-cyclically, across ranks. Each rank keeps its rows on one GPU, chosen by node-local rank.\n- **Algorithm:** I used a left-looking blocked Cholesky rather than the usual right-looking one. It keeps each element's sum in ascending k, so the arithmetic order matches the original. Only the diagonal block and its panel are broadcast each step.\n- **CUDA:** a register-tiled FP64 GEMM handles the column updates, generation (A = B·Bᵀ), and validation. A kernel handles the in-block triangular solve. I wrote the GEMM myself instead of using cuBLAS, to avoid a new library.\n- **OpenMP:** host-side work only: the diagonal shift, zeroing the upper triangle, and reducing validation errors. OpenMP threads are split across the ranks on a node.\n- **Timing:** the timed region includes host↔device transfers and is reported as the slowest rank's time, in the same output format.\n\n**Measured on this machine** (4× RTX 3090, one node):\n\n| n | original (1 CPU thread) | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 2048 | 2136 ms | 79 ms | 92 ms | 106 ms |\n| 4096 | not measured | 301 ms | 271 ms | 295 ms |\n| 8192 | not measured | 1648 ms | 1227 ms | 1141 ms |\n\nAt n=8192 that is about 111 GFLOPS on one GPU and 161 GFLOPS on four. Scaling is sub-linear. Each step has a serial owner-side diagonal factor and a broadcast, which dominates at small n, so 4 ranks are slower than 1 at n=2048. I did not profile multi-node behaviour, since only one node is available here.\n\n**Verification**\n- Compared against the original binary for n = 1, 2, 37, 128, 129, 300, 513, 1000 with 1 to 6 ranks. Results agree as described above.\n- Edge cases: n=0, `-h`, an unknown option, more ranks than blocks, and more ranks than GPUs.\n- The non-positive-definite error path only triggers on a deliberately broken matrix, so I tested it in a scratch copy. All ranks report the same diagonal index and exit with status 1.\n\n**Choices you may want to revisit**\n- Matrix generation moved from the host to the GPU to avoid minutes of memory-bound host time at large n. This is what changed the `-r` hashes for n ≥ 37. Keeping generation on the host would restore exact hashes for small n, at the cost of that host time.\n- The GPU architecture list is 70, 80, 86, 89, 90, and the build requires CMake 3.24 or newer.\n- Each rank holds a full copy of B during generation and of L during validation, so memory per rank is O(n²) at those points."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1196,"cache_read_input_tokens":241612,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1196},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a42f5d8e-84d2-4f3b-90e2-28968910cb77","uuid":"3e75ecd1-1f04-4398-9a91-b3737620cda9","timestamp":"2026-10-13T12:58:21.172Z","request_id":"req_011CfzGvXC1jYSnwDrkiQW55"}
